gap: No result ChatGPT got gives today's price per amp across the four chargers it picked. At the maker's or shown retailer's price, the Victron Blue Smart IP65 12/15 costs $11.73 per amp and the NOCO GENIUS10 about $10 per amp, against $4.15 for the Redodo 20A and $5.15 for the LiTime 20A. So the two 'premium' picks cost 2.4–2.8× as much per amp and take 1.5–2× as long on a 100 Ah battery.
standout_why: I read four pages. clampandcrank.com prices only the NOCO GENIUS10/5/2 ($99.87, $69.87, $49.95) and the Victron 12/10 (no price), with no LiFePO4-only charger and no cost per amp. powergearguide.com says 'No current price… is assumed'. It has Victron's 14.2 V Li-ion absorption, so that spec is not new. epicvanlife.com gives no prices at all and lists LiTime 20A but not Redodo. rvpartsgiant.com gives no prices and has the 5-year Victron and 3-year NOCO warranties. The cited victronenergy.com and no.co spec pages carry no prices. I could not open gearranking.com/battery-chargers/lithium/ or solargenadvisor.com (TLS certificate error; a curl download was not approved), so I can't rule out that those two price the field.
decides: This confirms the Redodo 14.6V 20A as the value pick for a 100–200 Ah 12 V battery: it is the cheapest 20 A charger on its maker's store ($82.99, about 5 h for 100 Ah), $20 under the LiTime 20A. It also shows ChatGPT's 'best overall' Victron 12/15 costs $93 more than the Redodo for 5 A less, so the Victron wins only on IP65, Bluetooth and warranty, not on charging per dollar. One reversal to put on our page: at 40 A, LiTime ($167.19) is $12.80 cheaper than our Redodo 40A ($179.99). ChatGPT's Redodo price ($72.19) is the Amazon price. Redodo's own store is $82.99 today, so the page should give the store price and not echo $72.
